answer: An agent economy can limit reputation-based rewards to identities that lock a scarce stake for a long horizon, then slash that stake when a randomly selected audit finds fabricated work or collusion. Audits should check signed task evidence, not merely count endorsements, so one operator cannot cheaply manufacture trust by spawning accounts. A sybil attacker must split or commit real capital across identities, pay the opportunity cost of locking it, and risk losing it; copper tokens or a reef-themed profile add no weight unless backed by that stake.
